ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, agents, and UBOs against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU Financial Sanctions Database, and the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Sanctions Register; mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) checks using Dow Jones Risk & Compliance or World-Check; enhanced due diligence and ongoing transaction monitoring under the AML/CFT Act 2009 (ss. 10–16A) applicable to the reporting entities involved in Steam Valve and PlayStation Store payment flows.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All company names must use Latin alphabet characters; Māori orthographic marks such as macrons and diacritics are permitted only as part of an approved Māori word; CJK and other non-Latin scripts are prohibited; the proposed name must not be identical or similar to any name already reserved or registered, and the Companies Office applies an exact-match and phonetic similarity review.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejection notice issued by the Registrar may be contested by filing a Notice of Review with the New Zealand Companies Office within 15 working days of the notice, specifying the legal and factual grounds of appeal; the appeal proceeds as an administrative reconsideration by the Registrar, and further recourse lies by way of an application for judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for this low-risk digital video game publishing entity (ISIC 5820 / Steam and PlayStation digital store publishing) provided that a physical registered office and agent are maintained in New Zealand through a licensed address-service provider, and that all statutory records are accessible; non-resident companies claiming tax-exempt status must additionally demonstrate commercial substance such as the maintenance of a dedicated bank account, operational governance documentation, and arm's-length contractual arrangements with platform operators.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate risk: 25% – unannounced on-site inspections may be undertaken where non-resident tax-exempt status is claimed and where ISIC 5820 digital revenue is sustained; New Zealand regulators periodically verify substance in targeted reviews of international companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand): ss. 12–19 (registration requirements), s. 24 (application for registration), s. 25 (issue of certificate of incorporation), s. 37 (authority to issue shares), ss. 81–89 (company registers), s. 126 (registered office), ss. 128A, 151–153 (board composition and director residency), ss. 161–165 (first board meeting and director duties); Companies (Proceedings) Regulations 1994; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (not applicable to a private international company); Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993 (for game classification).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), as administered through the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form 2) submitted online through the Companies Office (NZBN) portal, accompanied by Consents to Appointment of Officer (Form 4) and Consents to Appointment of Director (Form 5), together with an executed memorandum and articles / Constitution of the Company (if a custom constitution is adopted) and an NZBN designation request.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Under sections 37 and 38 of the Companies Act 1993, shares may be issued and paid for in money, property, or services, and may remain partly paid. No escrow account, government deposit, or capitalisation threshold is required for the incorporation or ongoing operation of an International Company limited by shares in New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the "Company"), passed in writing pursuant to Section 91 of the Companies Act 1993 on [DATE], at the registered office of the Company, namely [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS, NEW ZEALAND]. IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: That the subscription agreements dated [DATE] be and are hereby approved, and that the Company allot and issue an aggregate of one thousand (1,000) ordinary shares at a par value of NZD 0.01 each to the subscribers listed in the register of members, credited as fully paid, with any excess consideration recorded as a share premium reserve; the directors or their appointed attorneys are authorised to execute all allotment instruments and issue share certificates accordingly. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company be established at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], New Zealand, effective immediately, in compliance with Section 126 of the Companies Act 1993, and that the Company's statutory registers and records of account be kept at that address. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That [NAME] (passport no. [•]) be and is hereby appointed as sole director of the Company, and [NAME] (passport no. [•]) be appointed as company secretary, each to serve until removal or retirement in accordance with the Constitution; and that the appointed directors be and are hereby vested with the full board authority to open corporate bank accounts, negotiate and execute publishing agreements with Valve Corporation (Steam) and Sony Interactive Entertainment (PlayStation Store), and to do all acts necessary to carry on the business of digital video game publishing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — online name availability search and name reservation facility, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed company name through the NZBN/Companies Office online portal. The Registrar will reject any name that is identical or almost identical to an existing registered name, a restricted name, or one that contravenes sections 22, 23, or 24 of the Companies Act 1993 (e.g., names suggesting a connection with the Crown or that would mislead the public). Reserve the approved name for a period of 20 working days if incorporation will not be completed on the same day. Ensure the proposed name does not contain the words 'Limited' or 'Tapui' without lawful authorisation, unless the entity is to be registered as a limited liability company.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to 3 alternatives)
Directors' and shareholders' identification summary (passport copies may be requested later)
Notice of intent if using a restricted word (e.g., 'Trust', 'Bank', 'University')
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for review with the Registrar under section 23 of the Companies Act 1993, or immediately resubmit a substituted name avoiding the conflict. The Registrar will reissue a decision within 2 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Shareholder Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Subscribers; notarised by a New Zealand notary or qualified solicitor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and adopt a bespoke Constitution of the Company under section 28 of the Companies Act 1993, defining the share rights, board composition, quorum, reserved matters, and transfer restrictions consistent with the protected international company structure. Alternatively, the Company may operate without a constitution, in which case the default rules of the Companies Act 1993 apply. For a non-resident International Company, insert protective provisions regarding non-resident ownership, share transfer pre-emption rights, and elimination of the requirement for an annual meeting (permitting written resolutions under section 122). Execute the Constitution by all subscribers and arrange for notarisation and apostille certification, if required by the international publisher (Steam/PlayStation) or banking counterparties.
required_dossiers: Draft Constitution / Memorandum of Incorporation
Shareholders' subscription agreement
Notarised certificate of subscriber identification (for foreign shareholders)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any constitutional clause (e.g., if a clause purports to exempt directors from liability contrary to section 169), amend the offending provision and file a revised Constitution. No re-notarisation is required if the amendment is made by unanimous written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Consents to Appointment of Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Overseen by the incorporating agent and the first director; without prejudice to the NZ Companies Office filing requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form 4 (Consent to Appointment of Officer) and Form 5 (Consent to Appointment of Director) for each proposed director and officer. At least one director must be either a New Zealand resident or a director resident in an enforcement country in order to comply with section 151(2) of the Companies Act 1993, or alternatively a resident director exemption applies for single-director International Companies if a New Zealand-based agent holds the registered office. Attach a certified copy of each appointee's passport or driver licence and proof of residential address issued within the last three months. Consents must be signed by the appointee in their personal capacity and witnessed.
required_dossiers: Form 4 — Consent to Appointment of Officer (executed by each officer)
Form 5 — Consent to Appointment of Director (executed by each director)
Certified passport / national identity document copies
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement), notarised if issued outside New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects a consent for incompleteness or an unmet residency requirement, procure a supplementary statutory declaration or appoint an additional New Zealand-resident director and resubmit the affected Form 4/5 within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Registration (Form 2) and Payment of Incorporation Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, online via the NZBN Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of a Company (Form 2) electronically, providing the proposed company name, address of the registered office (which must be in New Zealand and not be a PO Box), the full name and residential address of each director, the intended business scope ('publishing of computer games for PC and console through digital stores'), and the share structure. Indicate the number and class of shares to be issued, the nominal value, and the total consideration payable. Pay the statutory incorporation fee of NZD 105.90 (including GST) by approved electronic payment; the fee approximates USD 66 at prevailing conversion rates. The system will automatically propose a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and prompt the creation of an IRD registration dataset.
required_dossiers: Form 2 — Application for Registration of a Company
Form 4 — Consent to Appointment of Officer
Form 5 — Consent to Appointment of Director
Executed Constitution (if custom) — uploaded as PDF
Record of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of deficiency under section 24(3) of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant must remedy the defect within 10 working days by filing an amended Form 2 or supplementary declarations. If the application is declined due to an omitted consent, obtain the missing signature and re-file; the fee will not be forfeited if the application is amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; automatic data sharing with Inland Revenue (IRD) and Statistics NZ.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful verification, the Companies Office issues the Certificate of Incorporation under section 25 of the Companies Act 1993, containing the date of incorporation, the company number, and the NZBN. The certificate serves as conclusive evidence of due incorporation. The Registrar automatically transmits the registration data to Inland Revenue for provisional income tax and GST account creation (utilised in Stage 3), and the entity becomes immediately eligible to enter into commercially binding agreements with Valve Corporation (Steam Works) and PlayStation Partner Program. Verify the electronic certificate on the NZBN portal and download the organisational extract.
required_dossiers: Official Certificate of Incorporation (downloadable PDF)
NZBN extract / public company extract
Companies Office registration receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within the service standard, contact the Companies Office business registrar via its dispute resolution line; any typographical error in the company number or name is corrected by filing a Notice of Correction, free of charge, with a turnaround of 1 working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation First Board Meeting, Register Establishment, and Allotment Recordation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; corporate secretary; New Zealand Companies Office for any subsequent change filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board (or have the directors pass the Pro Forma First Board Resolution set out above). Cause the company secretary to open and maintain the statutory registers required under sections 81–89 of the Companies Act 1993: the register of members, register of directors and officers, register of charges, and the company records. Allot shares in accordance with the subscription resolution, issue physical share certificates, and record the allotment in the register of members. Under current New Zealand law, a share allotment return does not need to be filed with the Companies Office for private companies; however, the registered office address must be separately confirmed in the online register. Execute and bank the publisher agreements with Steam and PlayStation Store under the board authority delegated to the directors.
required_dossiers: Minutes of First Board Meeting or written resolution
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Register of Members and Register of Directors
Registered Office Address Notification (filed electronically)
Authorized signatory list for Steam/PlayStation payout accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any defect in the statutory registers is identified by an auditor or the Registrar, rectify the entry within 5 working days by making a corrective minute and, where applicable, filing a Notice of Change of Particulars with the Companies Office. Delays in adjudicating the register of charges are cured by filing the instrument with the Registrar under section 149.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Classification Office (Te Mana Whakaatu) and the Film and Video Labelling Body (FVLB), established under the Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993; together with the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment for digital market compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993 — Labelling Compliance Certificate for Computer Game(s) (U/LL/R13/R15/R16/R18 classifications) and, where applicable, the FVLB Authorisation to Publish a Computer Game via an Electronic Network.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — No Environmental Impact Assessment required. Digital software publishing falls outside Schedule 1 of the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA) and does not constitute a 'project' or 'development' requiring a full EIA report. The activity is categorised as a zero-discharge, wholly online commercial service, thereby exempt from notification or consent under RMA ss. 9, 14 and 15.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in the ordinary course of digital publishing. The Company has zero point-source wastewater discharge, zero stationary combustion, and no VOC-emitting processes or hazardous waste streams. If the Company later operates warehousing or physical logistics for boxed products within New Zealand, it must comply with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, the Ministry for the Environment EnviroMark standards for e-waste, and the New Zealand Standard NZS 9201 for solid waste handling; at such time, an assessment under the RMA waste-management provisions and payment of the Waste Disposal Levy would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) compliance inspection is required if the Company occupies any physical commercial premises; a current Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004 must be displayed for leased office space. For the digital-only publishing business, no hazardous-substance licence or civil-defence certification is triggered. Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, WorkSafe NZ requires the Company to adopt a health and safety management system, conduct a workplace risk assessment, and ensure employee engagement in safety protocols; a clearance certificate is not normally issued, but the Company must register any workplace with FENZ if a scheduled substance is stored, which does not apply to cloud-based publishing. If office premises are used, the Company must maintain a Civil Defence emergency plan and fire-fighting equipment serviced in accordance with the FENZ Fire Safety and Evacuation of Buildings Regulations 2006.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), New Zealand Government; online portal: myIR Secure Online Services (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Border and export declaration clearance is administered by the New Zealand Customs Service (Ngā Ratonga Tiaki O Aotearoa) via the Trade Single Window (TSW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine registration duty. The CK_IC International Company is classified under the Tax_Exempt_Zone model for income tax purposes on its offshore digital publishing revenue, but must hold an IRD number and register for GST if it supplies remote services (digital game downloads via Steam and PlayStation Store) to New Zealand-resident consumers exceeding NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period. Step 2: Obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) if the entity is incorporated in New Zealand or registered as an overseas company on the New Zealand Companies Register under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993. Step 3: Apply for an IRD number for a non-resident company using form IR742 (Non-Resident Company Application for IRD Number), lodged through myIR or by post, accompanied by certified constitutional documents, registered office or service address, director and ultimate beneficial ownership information, and any certificate of exemption status supporting the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification. Step 4: Register for GST using form IR356 (GST Registration) or the combined non-resident IRD/GST application available in myIR, selecting the taxable period (one-month, two-month, or six-month) and designating the New Zealand settlement bank account for refunds. Step 5: Where physical export of console discs or collector's editions occurs, obtain a New Zealand Customs customer code and register as an exporter via the Trade Single Window to lodge export declarations. Step 6: Submit the application and await formal confirmation; the IRD issues the IRD number and GST registration number within 5-10 working days of a complete application, after which statutory filing obligations commence from the effective registration date selected by the applicant.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. The available statutory elections for a non-resident digital publisher in New Zealand are: (1) voluntary GST registration where the NZD 60,000 threshold is not exceeded (s 51(3), Goods and Services Tax Act 1985), permitting input tax credit recovery at the 15% rate; (2) election to use a one-month taxable period for GST where the person is in a net refund position, while aggregation is mandatory for registered persons whose taxable supplies exceed NZD 24 million per annum (s 15, GST Act 1985); (3) GST group election to consolidate two or more NZ GST-registered entities into a single registration (s 55, GST Act 1985); (4) hybrid mismatch designatory elections under Part 5B of the Income Tax Act 2007 (inserted by the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018), allowing ordering elections or de-application of hybrid mismatch rules for structured arrangements involving offshore trust or controlled foreign company interests; (5) the Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, which is available only to NZ-resident close companies and is therefore unavailable to the CK_IC; and (6) election under the CFC and FIF rules to attribute income from a non-resident entity, applicable only if the CK_IC were to be re-characterised as an NZ-resident entity, which is not the intended position under the exempt status certificate. For the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification, the operative mechanism is the written election for exempt status filed with the Commissioner of Inland Revenue, accompanied by the legal opinion and constitutive documents supporting the International Company structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by the Inland Revenue Department; cross-border digital services are subject to the offshore supplier registration rules (s 54A, GST Act 1985) and the remote services provisions (s 8(7) and s 11A, GST Act 1985).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 for suppliers carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand (s 51, GST Act 1985); for non-resident offshore suppliers of remote services, the registration threshold is NZD 60,000 of remote services supplied to New Zealand-resident consumers in a 12-month period (s 54A, GST Act 1985). Digital store sales via Steam and PlayStation Store must be aggregated across the NZ market; registration is mandatory once the projected or actual 12-month turnover exceeds the threshold, and voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. There is no separate low-value goods threshold for the CK_IC supplier, and the 15% GST applies to each NZ-resident consumer transaction from the first dollar once the entity is registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no pre-clearance API regime for electronic invoices. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol interoperability framework administered by the New Zealand Government's e-Invoicing Service. Tax invoices must nevertheless satisfy s 24 of the GST Act 1985, including supplier name and IRD number, GST registration number, issue date, description of the supplies, GST-exclusive and GST-inclusive amounts, and, for zero-rated exports, a statement of zero-rating. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR or via IRD-approved gateway software using machine-to-machine APIs; however, these APIs transmit summary return data, not invoice-level clearance. For Steam and PlayStation Store publishing, the payment rails (Steam Valve Payout and PlayStation Store Payout) do not impose any New Zealand GST withholding; the CK_IC, as the electronic supplier, must self-assess and return GST on supplies to NZ consumers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under s 11(1)(c) of the GST Act 1985 for goods physically exported by the supplier within 28 days of supply, and under s 11A for remote services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not electronically supplied for direct use in New Zealand and do not relate directly to New Zealand land or moveable property. For PC and console game publishing via Steam and PlayStation Store: (i) digital-store sales to non-NZ-resident end users qualify as zero-rated remote services if the supplier retains robust evidence of non-resident status, including IP-country geolocation, payment-card billing country, storefront country settings, and device telemetry; (ii) physical exports of console discs, cartridges, or collector's editions qualify only if the goods are exported within 28 days and the supplier holds transport and customs documentation; (iii) platform-store configuration fees charged to overseas developers may qualify for zero-rating under s 11A(1)(k) (services supplied to a person not resident in New Zealand) unless the services relate directly to New Zealand assets or are performed in New Zealand. Sales to NZ-resident consumers are subject to the standard 15% GST rate and cannot be zero-rated, even where the consumer uses the game outside New Zealand, because the supply is made to a person in New Zealand in the course of an e-commerce transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (TSW), including tariff classification HS 9504.50 for console games and the exporter customer code
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing physical export and clearance from New Zealand within the statutory 28-day window
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 from the New Zealand settlement bank evidencing receipt of export consideration from Steam Valve Payout or PlayStation Store Payout
Commercial invoice and signed publishing agreement / purchase order identifying the overseas customer, the specific game title, platform, and territory
GST export certificate (IR 372 form) certifying export and confirming no diversion of the goods back into the New Zealand customs territory

Digital evidence pack for zero-rated remote services: platform sales reports from Steamworks and PlayStation Partner Centre showing consumer-country breakdown, IP-geolocation logs, payment-card country codes, and time-stamped download records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department actively audits GST zero-rating through its GST refund and export verification programme, cross-matching New Zealand Customs Service export declarations against GST returns and bank inward remittance records by using the Business Intelligence and trade data reconciliation system. Where zero-rating is incorrectly claimed, the consequences include: (1) reinstatement of the full 15% GST as output tax on the supply, with the Commissioner reassessing the relevant taxable period retrospectively; (2) use-of-money interest (UOMI) on the unpaid tax at the IRD prescribed quarterly rate for underpayments; (3) shortfall penalties under Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 of 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for an unacceptable tax position, and 150% for evasion or an abusive tax position; (4) late payment penalties of 1% at the due date and a further 4% after seven days of unpaid GST; (5) for physical goods diverted or re-imported without complying with the 28-day export rule, the zero-rating is voided ab initio and the supplier must account for output tax even though the customer is a non-resident; (6) fraud or false documentation exposes the responsible persons to criminal liability under s 143A and s 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 with fines of up to NZD 50,000 for a first offence and NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences, and imprisonment of up to five years for wilful tax evasion; and (7) the general reassessment period is four years, extended to seven years where the shortfall arises from evasion or fraud, allowing the Commissioner to claw back historically zero-rated export claims. Digital publishers must retain the complete zero-rating evidence pack for at least seven years after the end of the taxable period (s 24(6), GST Act 1985); absence of the mandated documentation automatically triggers reinstatement of output tax plus penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua) is the apex monetary authority and prudential supervisor of registered banks. New Zealand does not operate a permit-based exchange-control authority; the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) separately screens sensitive foreign direct investment, and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) regulates FX derivative dealing and swaps under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. AML/CFT supervision is jointly exercised by RBNZ, FMA, and the Department of Internal Affairs under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no restrictions on the purchase, sale, remittance, or retention of foreign exchange. Software licensing royalties, Steam/PlayStation store proceeds, dividends, and interest may be repatriated without FX-authorization hurdles. The only payable frictions are statutory tax compliance: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at 15% on royalties absent a treaty reduction, approved issuer levy (AIL) on eligible interest, and resident withholding tax/international tax reporting. A profit-remittance 'hurdle' is therefore tax documentation (IRD tax compliance certificate, exemption certificate, double-tax-agreement residency certificate), not exchange control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, no minimum conversion ratio, and no deadline for repatriation or conversion. Exporters and digital-content sellers may hold USD, JPY, EUR, or other foreign currency proceeds in NZ or offshore accounts indefinitely. Banks nevertheless apply AML/CFT transaction reporting for cross-border inflows/outflows exceeding NZD 10,000, and the RBNZ may collect balance-of-payments statistical data on large direct, portfolio, and derivative cross-border positions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Settlement Account in NZD/USD multi-currency
Operational Account with USD/JPY clearing capability
Capital Escrow Account and Corporate Operational Account
Operational Account with SWIFT MT103 and foreign currency demand deposit capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - only if the EMI holds a New Zealand or equivalently regulated overseas e-money licence and offers physical or swift-based account rails. Wise (NZ entity), Airwallex, and Payoneer can onboard remote international companies, but their viability for CK_IC is conditional: they do not provide credit or escrow services, may restrict tax-transparent structures, and are not suitable for receiving Steam/PlayStation merchant payouts unless the publisher contract permits payouts to a third-party EMI account. Legal constraints under NZ AML/CFT require the EMI to conduct enhanced due diligence on non-resident companies, but do not prohibit onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch attendance is not a statutory mandate under New Zealand AML/CFT. Registered banks will typically accept remote onboarding where directors and beneficial owners pass electronic identity verification, LivenessCheck, sanctions/PEP screening, and certified-company-document review. In practice, a branch visit or notarized/legalized certificate of incumbency is requested for an offshore International Company with a tax-exempt status, non-resident directors, and no audited financials. The treasury plan should therefore prepare a remote-capable KYC pack while retaining a designated local director or professional corporate-service-provider representative for physical interviews if the bank triggers Enhanced Due Diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with no New Zealand business address, no substance, and tax-exempt classification is treated as a 'tax-haven-connected' legal vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, register of directors and shareholders, current beneficial ownership schedule, IRD tax compliance information (including exemption ruling if applicable), economic-substance rationale memorandum, Steam/PlayStation publishing contracts, development and trademarks to demonstrate genuine business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for injected capital from non-resident shareholders cannot be fully explained.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or accountant-certified financial statements of direct shareholders, underlying private-equity or venture-financing agreements, bank statements showing the liquidation path of capital, tax returns, gift/deed of trust if applicable, and a notarized source-of-wealth statement from each 25%-or-more owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to Valve/Steam and Sony PlayStation are recurring royalty/commission payments that may be characterized as related-party transfers or disguised profit repatriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed localization and publishing agreements with Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment; itemized income statements; platform payout summaries; transfer pricing documentation (if any related party is involved); purpose codes and commercial invoices; evidence of arms-length negotiation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person (PEP), or adverse-media flags on directors, authorized signatories, or beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions-screening report (OFAC/EU/UN/NZ), PEP disposition letter, professional legal opinion on screening accuracy, resignation/substitution plan for flagged individuals, and comprehensive corporate governance policy confirmation with bank-approved remedial controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions should be routed as SWIFT MT103 wires from the parent shareholder's bank to the NZ bank account in NZD, with a clear remittance information field reading 'EQUITY CAPITAL INJECTION – CK_IC' and the IFM/BoP purpose code 'Capital contribution in cash' (BoP code 2100 under NZ statistical conventions). The NZ receiving bank requires a board resolution authorizing account opening and the capital injection, UBO verification, and proof of source of funds of the sending account. No exchange-control approval is required. All inflows above NZD 10,000 are subject to AML/CFT screening and may be included in RBNZ balance-of-payments reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For Steam Store payouts and PlayStation Store payouts, disbursement flows are platform-initiated ACH/SEPA/SWIFT transfers into the CK_IC corporate account; onward payments to engine licensors, royalties, and contractors should use SWIFT MT103 or local ACH rails. A Commercial Letter of Credit is only appropriate for physical goods (console discs, peripherals, marketing print), not digital software licenses; nevertheless, an MT700-based LC may be obtained for key physical procurement from Asia. Purpose codes for outgoing royalties use 'Royalties and licence fees' (service code 2008) for payment to Valve/Sony, while trade payments for hardware use 'Goods trade – general merchandise' codes aligned with the New Zealand Harmonised System and IRD foreign-payment reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: NZD/USD deliverable outright forward (plain vanilla) for platform revenue conversion
NZD/USD non-deliverable forward (NDF) with offshore banks unable to accept NZD settlement
NZD/JPY cross-currency swap or rolling FX swap for Sony/PlayStation JPY-denominated payouts
USD/JPY outright forward or put option to hedge Steam USD receipts against JPY developer expenses
European-style foreign-exchange options (NZD call/USD put and USD call/NZD put) under FMA dealer licensing or wholesale-investor exemptions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 working days after the anniversary date of incorporation; the Companies Office issues a reminder before the annual return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A notice of default is issued; failure to remedy within 20 working days exposes the company and each director to statutory offences carrying fines of up to NZD 10,000 and may result in removal from the New Zealand Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (mandatory only if the company is a large company or a Financial Markets Conduct Act reporting entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office; prepared in accordance with External Reporting Board standards.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the company's balance date; the financial statements must be sent to shareholders and, where required, filed with the Registrar within 20 working days after delivery to shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete or file financial statements on time is an offence; directors may be liable for fines up to NZD 10,000, and persistent non-compliance may support regulator action including deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 applies to companies with total assets exceeding NZD 60,000,000 or total revenue exceeding NZD 30,000,000, and to any company whose shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares validly require an audit under section 199 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS for Tier 1 reporting entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for Tier 2 entities; small non-reporting companies may apply the simplified accounting framework prescribed by the External Reporting Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner confirmation filing. The annual return confirms registered shareholder details; changes in significant controllers must be recorded in the company's significant controller register and filed with the Companies Office within 10 working days after the change. Share transfers must be duly recorded in the Register of Members when authorised.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350–US$800 per annum for registered office and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000–US$12,000 per annum for a small-to-mid publishing entity, excluding group audit complexity

stage_6.entry_description: Gross revenue from publishing activities, including Steam/PlayStation Store digital sales and microtransactions, before deductions.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only income with a New Zealand source; global digital platform revenue is apportioned where development/exploitation activities are performed; do not include foreign-source sales unless income is derived through a NZ PE.
